messages:
emma_cs: @customer_jordan thanks for the report — can you paste the exact timeline and any client logs? You mentioned duplicate billing and partial output on reconnect.
raj_eng: quick summary from my side: customer says they get a partial SSE payload, client reconnects, and then server generates the remainder but also replays earlier tokens -> duplicate billable tokens.
lisa_sre: saw similar pattern in other threads but this one mentions auth rotation during the reconnect window which is interesting.
customer_jordan: timeline: 2026-03-15 14:03 client starts stream (request_id=rx-47). It streams ~120 tokens then connection drops. Client automatically reconnects after 1s. We rotate auth token on our side (short-lived) right after drop. On reconnect we send last_event_id=evt-120 and request_id=rx-47. Server returned tokens 121..300 but also resent 1..120 partially, so we got duplicates and were billed twice. Logs attached (see snippet below).
emma_cs: can you attach the raw SSE fragments? Even a pasted excerpt helps.
customer_jordan: pasted fragment below (redacted):

```
# client side excerpt
-> GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-xl&request_id=rx-47
SSE: id: evt-001
SSE: data: {"delta":"Hello"}
...
SSE: id: evt-120
connection: dropped (tcp reset)

reconnect attempt 1s later
-> GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-xl&request_id=rx-47
header: Authorization: Bearer <new-short-token>
header: Last-Event-ID: evt-120
SSE: id: evt-001
SSE: data: {"delta":"Hello"}
...
SSE: id: evt-300
SSE: data: {"delta":"<end>"}
```

lisa_sre: the fact we see evt-001..evt-120 again implies server resumed without verifying idempotency for the request_id or checking the resume window for the old session. Rotation of auth token could have forced creation of a new session on the backend while the client intended to resume old one.
raj_eng: probable root causes:
- resume token (Last-Event-ID) was honored but session mapping uses auth-subject+session-id; token rotation meant subject changed or session not found -> server created a fresh session that replayed from earliest buffer
- client reuses request_id but server doesn't enforce global dedupe across session handoffs
- billing increments occur when tokens are re-emitted, even if duplicates

emma_cs: customer asks for repro steps and a short-term mitigation.
raj_eng: Repro steps we tried locally (minimal):
1) Start a streaming request with request_id=R.
2) Let server stream ~N tokens.
3) Close connection (simulate TCP reset).
4) Rotate auth token on client and retry GET with same request_id and Last-Event-ID set to last seen event.
Observed: server resumed but replayed earlier events.

raj_eng: snippet of server-side log aligning to their timestamps:

```
[2026-03-15T14:04:21Z] stream-start request_id=rx-47 user=acct-99 session=ses-A
[2026-03-15T14:05:46Z] conn-closed session=ses-A reason=tcp-reset
[2026-03-15T14:05:47Z] auth-rotate acct-99 token=tok-rotated
[2026-03-15T14:05:48Z] stream-reconnect request_id=rx-47 user=acct-99 session=ses-B resume_from=evt-120
[2026-03-15T14:05:48Z] replaying buffer session=ses-B from=evt-001 count=300
```

lisa_sre: note session changed from ses-A to ses-B despite same acct. That means session lookup failed during reconnect and we created a new session that pulled from persistent buffer or cache and served from earliest sequence.
customer_jordan: is there a way to avoid being billed twice? We immediately paused ingestion on our side but charges already happened.
emma_cs: short-term workaround:
- If you can, upgrade client to include a unique idempotency-key header for the overall user-visible generation (not per-connection). If server sees same idempotency-key within 2 minutes, it should return cached output without recharging. We'll enable that on platform side as an emergency rule for affected customers.
- Increase client backoff to 500ms->2s to reduce race with auth rotation.

raj_eng: medium-term fixes we propose:
1) Enforce dedupe by idempotency-key across sessions for a configurable time window.
2) Make resume semantics strictly tied to a stable session identifier (sticky session id in a cookie or resume token that survives auth rotation) — if auth subject changes we should reject resume and return explicit 'resume_not_supported' so client can handle.
3) Only bill when an event reaches 'committed' state on server (i.e., after generation is finalized). For partial tokens, emit non-billable interim deltas until finalization to avoid double-charge on replay.

lisa_sre: quick mitigation rolled out: adding a 60s grace dedupe where request_id or idempotency-key are checked across recent sessions. I'm starting the rollout to the customer region now.
deploy-bot: Rollout triggered: rollout-id=rb-992 region=us-west-2 canary=5% -> 50% -> 100%, started by lisa_sre at 2026-03-16T02:12:00Z

customer_jordan: thanks — can you confirm when dedupe is active for our account? We need a window where we can rollback if things break.
emma_cs: assigned action items:
- lisa_sre: complete dedupe rollout and confirm on this thread (ETA 2h)
- raj_eng: prepare server patch for explicit resume_not_supported error and idempotency enforcement (ETA EOD)
- emma_cs: coordinate billing remediation and offer credit if duplicate charges confirmed (taking ownership)

lisa_sre: can confirm dedupe rule active for acct-99 in us-west-2 as of 2026-03-16T04:10Z. We observed one replay attempt and the dedupe blocked billing. Please validate on your side and DM logs.
customer_jordan: validated — no duplicate charge from our end for the retry that happened after rollout. Thanks.
raj_eng: followup: we'll publish recommended client best practices in docs:
- always send idempotency-key per logical generation
- persist last_event_id + server_resume_token and retry with both
- on auth rotation, prefer to fetch a short grace token that maps to same backend session or wait for confirmation before reconnecting

emma_cs: closing loop: I've opened billing case #CS-7831 to credit the duplicate charge earlier this week and will update once processed. Thanks everyone for quick response :raised_hands:
